portal_hypertension.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is characterized by a complex pathophysiology driven by intertwined metabolic and hepatic pathways, enabling the identification of multiple therapeutic targets and a rapidly expanding drug development pipeline. This review summarizes the current and emerging therapeutic landscape for MASLD and discusses key challenges for clinical implementation. The imminent availability of several new therapies is expected to pose important clinical challenges, particularly in accurately identifying patients most likely to benefit. portal_hypertension.abstract: Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided techniques are increasingly applied in hepatology, including for tissue acquisition, vascular access, pressure measurement, and selected therapeutic interventions. However, adoption remains heterogeneous because of variability in technical approaches, devices, outcome definitions, operator expertise, and the quality of available evidence. portal_hypertension.abstract: Accuracy of Baveno criteria for avoiding endoscopy in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is uncertain, and systematic upper gastrointestinal endoscopy (UGE) may not be necessary. We evaluated Baveno VI criteria performance in this population and developed an alternative non-invasive rule to exclude esophagogastric varices of any grade, rather than high-risk varices (HRV). Patients with BCLC 0-C HCC and compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD) from Italian Liver Cancer (ITA.LI.CA) database, with available liver stiffness measurement (LSM), UGE, and blood tests within six months of diagnosis, were included. portal_hypertension.abstract: The spleen is an important peripheral immune organ, and splenomegaly (SM) is a common complication of portal hypertension. However, the regulatory mechanisms underlying splenic apoptosis remain poorly understood. A portal vein stenosis-induced SM model was established in Sprague-Dawley rats, using a sham-operated (SO) group as the control. Apoptotic changes in splenic tissue cells were evaluated using the terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling (TUNEL) assay, immunohistochemistry staining, quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) analysis, and western blot analysis. portal_hypertension.abstract: Clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) is the main driver of hepatic decompensation, and its early identification allows timely initiation of preventive therapies. The hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) is the current gold standard for assessing portal hypertension, but it may underestimate portal hypertension in conditions with a presinusoidal component. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided portal pressure gradient (EUS-PPG) measurement enables direct measurement of portal pressure and may overcome these limitations.
